statement: A cause of action must accrue to a party before they can be made a plaintiff.
supporting_quote: Hence no cause of action has accrued to the 3rd defendant against the 1st and 2nd defendants.

statement: A document marked subject to proof is admissible in evidence if the opposing party does not object to it.
supporting_quote: This principle is applicable even to Deeds, irrespective of section 68 of the Evidence Ordinance. (Siyadoris v. Danoris (1841) 42 NLR 311, Silva v. Kindersly (1914) 18 NLR 85, Seyed Mohomed v. Perera (1956) 58 NLR 246, Cinemas Ltd v. Sounderarajan [1998] 2 Sri LR 16 at 18, Hemapala v. Abeyratne [1978-79] 2 Sri LR 222, Wijeardena v. Ellawala [1991] 2 Sri LR 14 at 34-35, Kandasamy v. Sinnathamby [1985] 2 Sri LR 249 at 255) What I have stated above shall not be taken to mean that all documents the opposing party purportedly requires to be marked subject to proof must necessarily be proved by calling witnesses.

statement: The contract of tenancy comes to an end if the building is completely destroyed by the fire, but not if the tenant can still exercise many of his rights under the lease notwithstanding the partial destruction of the property.
supporting_quote: If the building is completely destroyed the contract comes to an end, even though the land remains

statement: In circumstances where strict adherence to the letter of the law would result in injustice, the Court should exercise its judicial discretion to temper the rigidity of the law, allowing the spirit of justice to prevail by granting a deserving litigant the relief to which he is entitled.
supporting_quote: It is my considered view that, in circumstances where strict adherence to the letter of the law would result in injustice, the Court should exercise its judicial discretion to temper the rigidity of the law, allowing the spirit of justice to prevail by granting a deserving litigant the relief to which he is entitled.

statement: A lessor is not entitled to receive any rental for the entirety of the lease period if they fail to hand over peaceful possession of the premises to the lessee.
supporting_quote: I am of the view that the Defendants are not entitled to receive any rental for the entirety of the lease period.

statement: A deed of gift can be accepted by the donee or their representative, and acceptance can be inferred from the circumstances, including possession of the property and conduct of the parties involved.
supporting_quote: The general principle is that a donation is a contract and acceptance of it by the donee is essential to clothe the deed of gift with validity. There is a natural presumption that every deed of gift is accepted. The law does not specify a particular form for acceptance of a deed of gift.

statement: A new point which was not raised in the issues or in the course of the trial cannot be raised for the 1st time in appeal, unless such point might have been raised at the trial under one of the issues raised, and the Court of Appeal has before it all the requisite material for deciding the point or the question is one of law and nothing more.
supporting_quote: In the case of Setha Vs. Weerakoon 49 NLR 225, it was held, “A new point which was not raised in the issues or in the course of the trial cannot be raised for the 1st time in appeal, unless such point might have been raised at the trial under one of the issues raised, and the Court of Appeal has before it all the requisite material for deciding the point or the question is one of law and nothing more.”

statement: A sham transaction is not a proper transfer, and the attendant circumstances can point to a constructive trust.
supporting_quote: Precisely, if there was no intention to act upon the notarially executed document, it is no proper transfer but a sham.

statement: The transferor is duty bound to adduce evidence to show that he did not intend to dispose of the beneficial interest of the property.
supporting_quote: Sec. 83 of the Trusts Ordinance specifically states that where the owner of the property transfers or bequeaths it, and it cannot reasonably be inferred consistently with the attendant circumstances that he intended to dispose of the beneficial interest therein, the transferee or legatee must hold such benefit for the owner or his legal representative.

statement: A judgment is not defective merely because the learned trial Judge has not set out answers to the points of contest in a numerical sequence, even though the reasoning of the judgment demonstrates that each of those matters has in substance been examined and resolved.
supporting_quote: What the law insists upon is the disclosure of the judicial reasoning that led to the conclusion, not a rigid adherence to the mechanical form of answering each point of contest by number.

statement: A co-owner can sue a trespasser to have their title to the undivided share declared and for ejectment of the trespasser from the whole land.
supporting_quote: Any co-owner, or a party claiming under such a co-owner, is entitled to eject a trespasser from the whole of the common property,

statement: In a possessory action, the plaintiff need not prove lawful title to the subject matter of the action.
supporting_quote: I therefore hold that the Court of Appeal has erred when it held that the Plaintiff in order to institute this action should prove that the Plaintiff herself had lawful title.

statement: A legal objection can be raised at any time during the pendency of an action or appeal.
supporting_quote: A party to an action cannot present a case at the trial or inquiry materially different from what he has placed on record. (Ranasinghe v. Somawathie [2004] 2 Sri LR 154, Hildon v. Munaweera [1997] 3 Sri LR 220, Gnananathan v. Premawardane [1999] 3 Sri LR 301)

statement: A claim for prescriptive rights must fail if there is significant doubt about when or how continuously the alleged use occurred.
supporting_quote: Thus, it is the Defendant’s contention that even if there were occasional or incidental uses of the land which the Defendant does not concede, these would not be sufficient to grant the Plaintiff a legal right-of-way.

statement: A written promise to pay a sum of money must be in writing, but no special form of writing is required, and the promise may be contained in one document or evidenced by more than one document or by an exchange of documents.
supporting_quote: For the purpose of constituting a written promise, contract, bargain or agreement no special form of writing is required.

statement: Acceptance is an element for the completion of a valid gift under Kandyan Law.
supporting_quote: Having considered the statutory framework, the classic texts, and the decided cases, I am of the view that, while Kandyan Law does not require acceptance in the formal or technical sense known to Roman-Dutch Law, acceptance is nevertheless an element for the completion of a valid gift under Kandyan Law.

statement: A transferee of yet undetermined rights is not a necessary party to a partition action.
supporting_quote: The transferee of the yet undetermined rights is not a necessary party to the action.

statement: A tenant cannot resist an application by a purchaser to be placed in possession of premises after a partition or sale under the Partition Law, even if the tenant has a valid tenancy.
supporting_quote: In such a case, the tenant cannot resist an application by the purchaser to be placed in possession of the premises.

statement: A court must investigate the title of all parties in a partition action, and a fresh trial should be ordered if the title has not been adequately investigated.
supporting_quote: The main purpose of the Partition Law fails at the end of the case.

statement: The plaintiff must include in the plaint all persons who, whether in actual possession or not, to his knowledge are entitled or claim to be entitled to any right, share or interest to, of, or in the land to which the action relates, whether vested or contingent, and whether by way of mortgage, lease, usufruct, servitude, trust, life interest, or otherwise, or to any improvements made or effected on or to the land.
supporting_quote: For instance, section 5 of the Partition Law enacts that the plaintiff in a partition action shall include in his plaint as parties to the action all persons who, whether in actual possession or not, to his knowledge are entitled or claim to be entitled to any right, share or interest to, of, or in the land to which the action relates, whether vested or contingent, and whether by way of mortgage, lease, usufruct, servitude, trust, life interest, or otherwise, or to any improvements made or effected on or to the land.

statement: A deed executed before a notary can be proved by the notary if they knew the executant personally and can testify that the signature on the deed is that of the executant.
supporting_quote: Where a deed executed before a notary is sought to be proved, the notary can be regarded as an attesting witness within the meaning of section 68 of the Evidence Ordinance if the notary knew the executant personally and can testify that the signature on the deed is that of the executant.

statement: A person can possess a property without occupying it, and to prove possession, it is not necessary to prove that he or she lives in the property or occupies it.
supporting_quote: One can possess a property without occupying the same. To prove possession it is not necessary to prove that he or she lives in the property or occupies the property.

statement: A landlord need not establish any grounds of ejectment stipulated in section 22 of the Rent Act No. 7 of 1972 for success in his suit for ejectment if the tenant has repudiated the tenancy.
supporting_quote: In such a case the landlord need not establish any one or more of the grounds of ejectment stipulated in section 22 of the Rent Act No. 7 of 1972 for success in his suit for ejectment.

statement: Section 404 of the Civil Procedure Code allows the court to admit parties as plaintiffs or defendants after affording a hearing to all parties to the action, in the case of assignment, creation or devolution of any interest in the subject matter of a pending action.
supporting_quote: That section gives the Court power to allow the assignee to be added as a party when the assignment was made at any time pending the action; and the Court ought to do so in a proper case when it appears convenient and possible without prejudice to the other party.

statement: Failure to cite the relevant section in a judgment does not vitiate the decision if it has not caused prejudice to the opposite party.
supporting_quote: It is a well-settled principle of interpretation that as long as an authority has power to do a thing, it does not matter if it purports to do it by reference to a wrong provision of law.
